title: BOX OF COALPORT CHINA, ETC
reason: Coloured batwing cups and saucers consistent with Coalport, plus other Victorian and Deco pieces, under-described as 'box of Coalport china, etc'.
findings: One photo. Five cups on saucers and a matching slop or sugar bowl in a 'batwing' pattern: solid cobalt or navy cloud-shaped panels on a white ground around the rims (3 navy, 1 red, 1 turquoise), with gilt floral sprays inside a couple of the pieces and moulded ribbed rims. This matches the design of Coalport batwing tea ware as I know it (late 19th or early 20th century style), which supports the title 'Coalport china', but no backstamp or pattern number is visible (undersides not shown), so the maker is unconfirmed. Also in the lot: two large brown-glazed oval meat or drainer platters with wall-hanging loops (maker unknown), two amber frosted pressed-glass octagonal plates with a moulded bird or fish motif (Art Deco style, unmarked), and about 12 small blue and white transfer-printed floral fluted plates (Victorian style, tea plate or butter pat size).
condition: No cracks or chips visible at this scale, but gilt wear and rim damage cannot be judged; colours look strong with no obvious fading.
rescore_note: Five harlequin batwing cups and saucers plus a slop bowl match Coalport batwing but no backstamp seen, so the maker is likely rather than certain; the Deco amber plates, brown platters and small blue and white plates add little. Judged $80 to $200 band. Not price-checked (search limit hit).
